newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo sees similar second half earnings.
newsitem.headline: Anglo sees similar second half earnings.

text.p: South Africa's largest company, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, said on Tuesday it expected similar earnings growth in the second half as in the first half of the year.

"Reflecting a slowing down in the economy domestically and, at best, only modest gains in commodity prices internationally, certain sectors in which the Corporation is invested are unlikely to perform strongly over the next six months," the company said in a statement with interim results.

"However, headline earnings for the second half are expected to be similar to those of the first half, so that headline earnings for the full year are expected to show real growth over the year ended 31 March."
Anglo reported headline earnings per share of 1,045 cents in the half year ended September 30 versus 860 a year ago. Total earnings were 1,273 cents against 837.0
Chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said South Africa faced difficulties but there was a risk of overstating short-term problems.
"The challenges of meeting targets set out in the government's sound Growth, Enmployment and Redistribution strategy announced in June remain daunting," he said.

"Domestic and foreign investors would clearly like faster progress on implementation, particularly in privatisation and the abolition of exchange control, as well an an effective programme to combat violent crime.
"However, too many South Africans have allowed short-term problems to have an excessive impact on confidence."
